Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call summary:
- Goals: integrate Redwood for customer-facing semantic search + assistant; support reranking with embeddings and structured tool-calling for transactions.
- Priority constraints: strict data residency (US), SSO/KMS for keys, and prompt governance for regulated content.

Open technical items (I captured the ones you asked us to follow up on):
1) SDK setup & auth: ACME prefers an OAuth2 flow with short-lived tokens and KMS integration for key material. You asked whether our SDK supports short-lived credentials and a KMS-backed signing flow.
2) Routing & model variants: you want low-latency path for transactional flows and cost-optimized batch for analytics. Need policy examples for routing by latency vs. cost.
3) Structured output / tool calling: example JSON schema + validation for payments + order APIs and how we handle tool calling/fallbacks.
4) Embeddings & reranker: sample workflow for embedding pipeline + reranker (FAISS vs. hosted reranker) and any latency/cost tradeoffs.
5) Prompt templates & governance: versioning prompts, preventing prompt injection, and red-team cadence for regulated prompts.

Attachments: I attached our lightweight SDK integration stub and a prompt governance checklist — these are starting points.

Proposed next steps: 
- Dylan & Dev: can you confirm feasibility and put together a short tech plan for items 1-4 (ETA: EOD tomorrow)?
- Marissa & ACME: Jordan/Alice, if you can confirm which flows are mission-critical (transactions vs. exploratory search) we'll prioritize latency SLOs.
- Security: ACME sec team, happy to set a separate call to walk through SOC 2/SAML/KMS details.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a proposed timeline once Dylan and Dev chime in.

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth: We must avoid long-lived static API keys for production. Ideally your SDK can exchange an OAuth client credential for a short-lived token and support our KMS for envelope encryption of any persistent secrets. Can you confirm support or outline a recommended pattern if not fully supported?

2) Routing: For the payments path we need tail latency under 250ms p50 and p95 under 600ms. For search/analytics we can accept higher latency if it cuts cost substantially.

3) Tool calling: We will provide an orders API (internal) that your tool-calling layer can invoke. We need a strict JSON schema and replay protection. What are your recommended validation hooks?

4) Prompt governance: We need a versioned prompt registry and an audit trail for which system prompts were used for a given transaction. Also want examples of prompt injection mitigations (context controls, tokenizer truncation, allowlist/denylist).

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the ping — here's a concise tech plan we can share with ACME. Happy to turn any section into a short doc.

1) SDK & Auth:
- We support short-lived bearer tokens via our token-exchange API. Pattern: customer issues a signed JWT (service-to-service) that our auth endpoint exchanges for a temporally-limited bearer token (TTL configurable). For KMS integration we support envelope encryption for persisted secrets; we can accept encrypted key blobs you manage with HMAC verification.
- If ACME prefers OAuth2 with full OIDC client flows, we can offer an integration pattern (requires minor config) or use internal token-exchange for server-to-server flows.

2) Routing & model variants:
- Policy examples: route by request.tag ("transaction") -> low-latency model cluster (p50 target ~150ms), otherwise route to cost-optimized batch endpoints.
- We expose per-route SLOs and autoscaling rules in the Dedicated/Private control plane; can pin model versions for transactional flows.

3) Structured output / tool calling:
- Recommend a strict JSON schema with a top-level metadata block (id, schema_version, timestamp, nonce) and an actions[] array. We validate outputs against the schema server-side before executing any tool call; replay protection via nonce + short TTL and server-side idempotency keys.
- Fallbacks: if validation fails, fall back to a safe read-only mode and surface the failure to the app.

4) Embeddings & reranker:
- Option A (hosted): Redwood-managed embedding index (FAISS) + hosted reranker for best relevance. Option B: customer-managed index with Redwood embedding pipeline.
- Latency/cost: hosted reranker gives better freshness and simpler ops at higher cost; FAISS with offline rerank provides lower unit cost but higher tail latency for fresh queries.

5) Prompt templates & governance:
- Versioned prompt registry: store prompts (id, version, hash, author, change log) in the control plane. Every request logs the prompt id+version used.
- Injection mitigations: context window controls (truncate user content to N tokens), allowlist/denylist for tools, model-agnostic sanitizers, response schema validation, and insert guard tokens in system prompts.
- Red teaming cadence: recommend initial red-team pass during onboarding, quarterly targeted injections for high-risk prompts, and automated fuzzing on new prompt versions.

Deliverables (ETA EOD tomorrow): a one-pager for ACME with the above plus a sample JSON schema for the orders tool-call and a short auth diagram.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in a few implementation notes from the infra side: 

- SDKs: We'll publish node/python/java examples showing token-exchange flows. The client will call our /token-exchange with a signed JWT; token TTL can be configured down to 5m for strict environments.
- KMS: We support customer-managed key blobs; optionally we can integrate with AWS KMS via cross-account grants in Dedicated/Private setups.
- Routing: config prototype: 
  route_rules:
    - match: request.attrs.path == "/payments"
      target: low_latency_cluster
      sla_target: p95 < 600ms
    - match: request.attrs.tag == "analytics"
      target: cost_optimized_batch

- Tool-calling: we'll provide a sample schema (attached) and a validation hook that returns a bind-safe response. Execution is gated by schema validation + idempotency keys.

I attached a small prototype schema for the orders tool (JSON stub). Happy to run a quick demo next week.
